more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the US.
US food use is subject to the listed CFR provisions and their conditions, checked in 2026.
more_info.overview: Calcium lactobionate is the calcium salt of lactobionic acid, made through oxidation of lactose. It is chemically different from calcium lactate or calcium gluconate. FDA describes its food function as a firming agent in dry pudding mixes. The permitted amount is the quantity needed to produce that technological effect.
more_info.origin: Manufactured by oxidising lactose to lactobionic acid and producing its calcium salt. The route uses a lactose starting material. The reviewed regulation does not identify the source of every commercial lactose feedstock or certify a product's dietary suitability.
more_info.uses: Used as a firming agent in dry pudding mixes. The US regulation permits the quantity required to produce that effect; it does not provide a general list of unrelated retail foods.
